summary: Request for verifiable audit export bundle (hourly checksums, RFC3161 timestamps, and legal chain-of-custody)
description: Finova requests a legally defensible hourly audit-export bundle for a 30-day window (2026-02-10T00:00:00Z to 2026-03-12T00:00:00Z). Requirements: 1) Each hourly bundle must include a monotonic sequence number per-tenant, per-event SHA-256 checksum for each object, and an HMAC-SHA256 over the entire bundle computed with a customer-scoped signing key. 2) Each bundle must be accompanied by an RFC3161 timestamp token for the bundle manifest. 3) A human-readable chain-of-custody CSV must list object keys, S3 ETags, size, SHA-256, KEK-wrapping key ID (KMS ARN), and the export job run_id. 4) Provide verification instructions and a signed manifest (manifest.json + manifest.sig) that third-party auditors can validate. Customer also requests evidence that late-arriving events were de-duplicated and an explanation for any gaps or sequence jumps.
impact: Customer requires evidence for an imminent regulatory audit (GLBA/PCI scope) — inability to supply timely, verifiable export puts audit milestone at risk and may delay certification. Finova flagged as enterprise SLA with audit escalation.
environment_description: Production tenant: finova-prod tenant_id=tn-0472. Export path: s3://redwood-exports/finova-prod/audit/2026-02-10_to_2026-03-12/. Exports are produced by the audit-exporter job (k8s namespace: export-runner, image: redwood/audit-export:v2.4.1). Signing keys are managed in customer-scoped KMS keyring (alias/finova-evidence).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer provided list of expected event IDs and time ranges (attached as sample_event_ids.csv).
2) Run adhoc export job with parameters: --tenant tn-0472 --start 2026-02-10T00:00:00Z --end 2026-03-12T00:00:00Z --bundle-size hourly --signing-key alias/finova-evidence --timestamp rfc3161
3) Verify generated manifest.json contains: bundle_id, start_ts, end_ts, sequence_number_range, sha256 per object, hmac, rfc3161_token reference, kms_wrapped_key_id.
4) Using provided public key, run: openssl dgst -sha256 -verify pubkey.pem -signature manifest.sig manifest.json (expect SUCCESS).

investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: non-monotonic sequences due to late-arriving events that were assigned sequence numbers out of order by the stream-ingestion service.

Checked exporter's manifest generator: v2.4.1 used MD5 for object integrity metadata alongside SHA-256 for content; HMAC used export-runner's ephemeral key instead of customer-scoped KMS wrapper in one code path (bug introduced in PR #721).

Found S3 lifecycle policy recently applied to a staging prefix which caused object copies used by intermediate dedup step to be GC'd earlier than expected (rule applied on 2026-02-27). This produced missing ETag evidence for some older hourly bundles.
Confirmed KMS wrapping performed correctly for final bundles: KEK ARN present and decryptable with customer's KMS grants (test decrypt executed by SRE under customer-approved cross-account role).

Computed independent SHA-256 for sample objects and matched against manifest SHA-256 after backfill (match confirmed). RFC3161 timestamp obtained from 3rd-party TSA (CompliantTSA) and embedded as timeStampToken in manifest.

Root cause summary: combination of (a) exporter code path using ephemeral hmac key for early candidate bundles and (b) inadvertent S3 lifecycle rule that removed intermediate artifacts needed for dedup verification.
resolution: Provided Finova a verified audit bundle containing hourly manifests for the requested window. Actions taken: 1) Re-ran backfill with --dedup=true and --signing-mode=kms-wrapped (run_id run-20260313-1530). 2) Generated signed manifest.json + manifest.sig; timestamped via CompliantTSA (RFC3161). 3) Uploaded final bundle to a secure S3 share and delivered verification instructions (openssl commands and KMS key ARN). 4) Documented the issue and opened INT-4512 to replace ephemeral HMAC path with customer-scoped KMS-wrapped HMAC v2 and to add a pre-export check for S3 lifecycle rules. Customer confirmed receipt and will validate with auditors; follow-up scheduled 2026-03-15.
